extracted.intended_audience: university faculty/administrators and mathematics educators designing or operating graduate/professional development programs for middle-school mathematics teachers
extracted.subtask_short: designing master's program for middle_school math teachers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive standards for structuring a 36–39 credit-hour master's/professional development program for middle-school mathematics teachers, including admissions tracks, curriculum, course formats, partnerships, evaluation, and logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program credit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Program is thirty-nine credit hours (36 course hours noted elsewhere for some variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify total credit hours required for degree; used to structure courses, tracks, and capstone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-track admission model (professional vs initial licensure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two tracks: professional track (requires initial license for those teaching middle school math) and initial licensure track (requires passing the Middle School Mathematics MTEL by the time first five math courses are completed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define admission criteria separately per track; make licensure/timing expectations explicit to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional track course requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Those entering the professional track must take all nine mathematics courses, three mathematics education courses, and a three-credit clinical experience in which the teacher implements an action research project in his or her classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require a coherent set of content + pedagogy + clinical action research for practicing teachers seeking professional development/licensure advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial license track course requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrollees must take the first five listed mathematics courses, choose two of the remaining four as mathematics electives, complete a MassDOE-approved kernel of three pedagogy courses, one mathematics methods course, and a student teaching practicum and seminar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance mathematics content with required pedagogy and practicum to meet initial licensure requirements without exceeding credit loads.

rubrics_metrics.name: No undergraduate-major requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no specific requirements for an undergraduate major for program admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow eligibility for non-math majors (focus on in-service teacher population), but be prepared to address mixed-background cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical experience with action research
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical experience (EDG992) is a three-credit course providing a full semester experience centered on an action research project designed and carried out in the teacher's classroom (prerequisite EDG852).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate action research into clinical practicum to connect program learning to classroom practice; sequence with a prior action research methods course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of course format and active pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: No required format for courses; instructors decide structure. Courses tend to include group work, discovery, hands-on activities, and lecture-discussion as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage active learning (group work, hands-on experiments), adapt format to class size (smaller classes favor discussion and group work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make mathematics relevant to middle school curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses should make clear connections between course mathematics and the middle school classroom; include assignments tying subject matter to strands in the Massachusetts Curriculum Frameworks and explicitly relate advanced topics to grade-level standards when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When course material exceeds middle-school standards, emphasize how doing higher-level mathematics improves understanding and teaching practice; include curriculum-mapping assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing mixed-background cohorts
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses were designed for non-math majors; when math majors enroll they may find much content familiar and mixed classes can be problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate mixed preparedness; consider revising course content or offering bridge/enrichment options to serve both math majors and non-majors effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate-level designation by approach and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses may include undergraduate content but are graduate-level because of the approach to the material and its application to middle school curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize depth of understanding, pedagogical application, and reflective/professional tasks to justify graduate credit for material overlapping with undergraduate topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course prefix and credit control
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a distinct course prefix (MSM) for middle-school-specific graduate courses to prevent students in other degree programs from counting them for degree credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish administrative mechanisms (prefixes/policies) to control credit applicability across programs; allow exceptions with approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program evaluation via alumni feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators collect alumni feedback via surveys measuring confidence in teaching mathematics, usage of course content in classrooms, career changes (e.g., supervisory positions), and licensure attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted survey questions and analyze responses (percent reporting increased confidence, classroom application, professional advancement) to inform curriculum adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and enrollment monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Track retention (program reports a 93% retention rate) and implement recruitment/outreach strategies to maintain enrollment; accept low-enrollment courses with case-by-case justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor cohort sizes, contact district leaders to recruit, schedule courses every-other-year when appropriate, and justify low-enrollment offerings based on program needs and community value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and community partnership strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote the program by contacting department heads and mathematics supervisors in local school districts and offering courses subsidized or scheduled to meet district needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop district partnerships, provide accessible course schedules and materials, and use local endorsements to sustain enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership and district support requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must teach in a district that agrees to partner with the university and have district administrative support; partner personnel review applications and make recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalize district partnerships and include district involvement in selection and support processes; provide stipends/substitute funding to reduce teacher barriers to participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial supports for participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds can waive tuition and fees, provide stipends for attending classes outside school day, and fund travel/subsistence and substitute teachers when classes meet during school days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure funding or institutional support to reduce participation costs and time barriers for in-service teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort-based 25-month program structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Program delivered in cohorts over 25 months: three summers plus two intervening academic years with a mix of on-site summer intensives and semester-length online/blended courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cohort scheduling to build community and leadership capacity; combine intensive on-site weeks with distance components to respect teacher schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blended course delivery model
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic-year courses are blended: a two-day on-campus component plus distance-education components using Blackboard, PC NoteTaker, email, and Adobe Connect; on-campus days meet eight hours each with nightly homework covering ~40% of course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design blended courses with concentrated face-to-face time and substantial online activities; ensure technology and support for synchronous/asynchronous components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summer institute intensive model
rubrics_metrics.description: On-site summer courses meet eight hours a day for five days a week (one- or two-week formats) with homework each evening, modeled after the Vermont Mathematics Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intensive summer institutes to deliver content-rich experiences that accommodate teachers' schedules and allow deep immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum guidance by national/state standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Curriculum and pedagogical goals are guided by The Principles and Standards (NCTM), The Mathematical Education of Teachers, and Foundations for Success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align course goals and outcomes with established national/state standards and teacher-education frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program course composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The 12-course program includes seven mathematics courses, one statistics course, three education courses, and a capstone integrating math and pedagogy; courses can be taken for either an MAT (specialization) or an MA degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a coherent mix of content, statistics, pedagogy, and integrative capstone options to support multiple degree pathways and professional goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capstone integration and degree choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Program culminates in a capstone (TEAC 889 or MATH 896) that integrates mathematics and pedagogy; participants may choose MAT with specialization or MA depending on department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer flexible capstone options tied to degree pathways and ensure capstone assesses integrated application of learned mathematics and pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research agenda for program assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Research focuses on how teachers translate mathematical knowledge and habits of mind into classroom practice and how changes in practice affect student achievement; includes studies on teacher leadership and uses value-added models to estimate effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate research components into the program to study effectiveness, use appropriate statistical methods, and publish findings to inform improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority focus on rural education
rubrics_metrics.description: Program gives priority to teachers from rural communities and adapts to rural definitions and contexts; special workshops (Rural Education Workshop) inform project design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor recruitment, scheduling, and supports to rural teachers' needs and contexts; include rural-focused research and professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology and tools in instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses integrate technology: TI-84 calculators (provided to participants), GeoGebra, MapleTA for online assessment, Excel, and other software to explore concepts and assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide hardware/software resources to participants and design activities that use technology to explore and assess mathematical concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course credit and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: All courses are three graduate credits; specific prerequisites are stated for some courses (e.g., MSM 703 prerequisite MSM 701; MSM 711 prerequisite MSM 701; MSM 713 prerequisite MSM 703; EDG992 prerequisite EDG852).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define credit value and prerequisite sequences clearly to ensure coherent progression through content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course topic and learning-objective specifications (mathematics courses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed course descriptions specify topics and emphases (examples): MSM 701 'Patterns, Relations, and Algebra' emphasizes multiple approaches to relationships; MSM 703 'Precalculus' develops firm understanding of functions; MSM 705 'Geometry and Measurement' covers measurement, transformations, and geometric proofs; MSM 707 'Number Systems' covers integers, rationals, reals, complex numbers, divisibility, congruence, Chinese Remainder Theorem; SM 709 covers data displays, measures, probability, regression; MSM 711 covers linear systems and matrices; MSM 713 covers fundamental calculus concepts; MSM 715 covers discrete mathematics topics and proof methods; MSM 717 surveys history of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify clear topic lists and learning objectives for each course that connect to middle-school teaching practice and provide instructors with content targets and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course topic and learning-objective specifications (pedagogy courses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pedagogy course descriptions: EDG850 analyzes historical, mathematical, and psychological influences in curricula; EDG851 explores strategies for diverse learners; EDG852 examines quantitative/qualitative methods for action research and requires designing an action research project; EDG992 is the clinical experience centered on action research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit pedagogical learning objectives including differentiation, research design, and clinically applied projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of action research into teacher development
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers design and carry out action research projects (EDG852) and then implement them in their clinical experience (EDG992), building research design skills (sampling, survey design, data analysis, validity, reliability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence coursework so that methods training precedes implementation; require applied, classroom-based research culminating in supervised clinical assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of courses and recommended scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a recommended sequence and schedule (example: MATH 800T, MATH 802T and TEAC 801, MATH 804T in spring & summer etc.; table given for cohort fourth sequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish a recommended course order and cohort schedule to facilitate planning and ensure prerequisites and capstone readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of formative assessment and online assessment tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of online assessment software (MapleTA) in courses and emphasis on using technology for assessment and exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt formative assessment tools appropriate for blended/online components and provide training/support for teachers using these tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit listing of resources and bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide annotated resources (texts, websites, lesson plan collections, journals) and cautions about quality of external sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curate and share vetted resources and links to support instructors and participants; annotate for classroom applicability and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of substitutes and schedule accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: When classes meet on school days, grant funds pay for teachers' substitutes; stipends support attendance outside regular school day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for replacement teacher coverage and compensation when scheduling professional development during the school day to remove barriers to teacher participation.
